exposure: time interval from myomectomy to pregnancy (TIMP)
cohort: The study included 4006 women who experienced first singleton births after their first laparotomic myomectomy, identified from the National Health Insurance Research Database and the Taiwan Maternal and Child Health Database.
finding: A time interval from myomectomy to pregnancy (TIMP) between 6 and 11 months is associated with lower risks of gestational hypertensive disorders and neonatal death compared to TIMP <6 months or >=12 months, especially for women over 35 years old.
followup_time: Up to 28 days post-birth (for neonatal death)
